All remaining ~260 differing rows are one systematic codegen-shape mismatch, verified unreachable with every available compiler (GC/1.3, 1.3.2, 2.0, 2.5, 2.7 all probed): for struct-member table indexing MWCC always reassociates to `add r3, r30, idx*4` + `lwz 0x7270(r3)`, while retail emits `addi r3, r30, 0x7270` + `lwzx r28, r3, idx*4`. I tested eight C spellings (member index, decayed pointer local, array-decay into `void**`, cast byte-pointer with explicit `<<2`, element index on a `void**` cast, direct symbol-relative access, and an inlined accessor taking base / byte-offset as parameters) — every one is folded identically by the 1.3 backend, so retail's address mode must come from a compiler build not in the probe set. Secondary residual rows: the int→float 2^52 magic is loaded from the compiler's private literal pool (`lis/addi; lfd 0(rX)`) instead of the module pool at `lbl_8_rodata_0+0x98`, and case 0's scratch-register permutation (cnt/0/1 in r5/r4/r3 vs retail r3/r5/r4). Note the case labels were corrected against the decoded jump table (`jumptable_8_data_7C34`: state 2→block at 0x2824, state 4→0x2818, state 33→0x2994, etc.), so the emitted table mapping now matches retail.

Best candidate is 64.5% (1216/3430 rows): the retail frame layout, all local offsets, conversion temp slots, and jump table now match GC/1.3.2 exactly, and the case bodies/calls are structurally faithful, but MWCC's callee-saved register assignment cannot be reproduced — retail keeps arg0=r26, &v174=r27, &v180=r28, &v18C=r29, &rodata=r30, &bss=r31 (rematerializing &v168), while this unit always yields arg0=r31, &rodata=r30, &v168=r29, &bss=r28, &v18C=r27, &v180=r26, &v174=r25 (with matching FPR permutations), and that assignment proved invariant to variable declaration order, parameter-list shape, aliasing the parameter, chained-assignment form, frame placement, and the 1.3/1.3.2/2.x compilers. The residual is therefore compiler-internal allocation/scheduling plus the literal-pool symbol difference (@171@ vs lbl_1_rodata_3180+0x58) that the oracle does not retarget.

Unit compiles and matches 37.3% of instruction rows (65.3% objdiff similarity, 1621/2584 rows still differ). The residual differences are dominated by non-volatile register allocation and frame layout: retail saves r17-r31/f22-f31 with a 0x140 frame while our (flattened, goto-based) reconstruction keeps fewer values simultaneously live, so it saves only r20-r31/f24-f31 with a 0x120 frame; every stack-relative access is consequently shifted by 0x20 and most operands use different registers. Fixing this requires the original nested-block source shape (longer live ranges) rather than further local edits.

Compiles at 73.8% (1629/2686 rows differ): all recovered control-flow shapes, early-exit jumps, frame locals and mis-lifted sites are now in place, but MWCC's global register allocation still diverges because the lift draft's invented vN/tN temporaries give different live ranges than the original source — retail holds arg0 in r31 and the data pointer in r14 with a 0x350 frame, ours colors arg0 r15, rodata r30, spills the data pointer to 0x30c and grows the frame to 0x380 with 0x30 bytes of fctiwz/int-conversion temporaries parked above the user local area.

Reconstruction is at 96.0% (67 of 1653 instruction rows differ); the function's structure, state machine, jump table, switch case lists, frame layout (0x290 with the five path/DVDFileInfo pairs), call sequence and all control flow now match. The residual rows are compiler-internal register allocation and scheduling choices that did not move under any of the tried source spellings: the manager pointer chosen as r3 (target) vs r4 (mine) across the result-code switches, the byte buffer kept in r6/r4 with a factored base pointer (addi r4,r31,0x220) in the state-7 header block vs r5/r31 offsets, one CSE'd manager reload in case 39 (fn_1_46B4's argument), and the rotlwi/rlwimi vs srwi/rlwimi lowering of the (M->unk_18<<16)|(M->unk_1C>>16) store at buf+0x7580.

Semantically complete, compiling reconstruction at 57.5%. The remaining 1597 differing rows are dominated by register/frame allocation that MWCC 1.3.x will not reproduce from editable source: the target keeps 18 callee-saved float registers (f31-f14, one per repeated push block plus block A's hoisted constants, frame 0x3E0 with locals+temps ending at 0x28F), while my identical C forces only 16 callee-saved floats and 80 fewer bytes of spilled temporaries (frame 0x370), so every fp-save offset, the GPR save base (0x270 vs 0x2C0) and the register names inside the 18 unrolled push blocks still differ; the early-section diffs (self in r30 vs r31, m in r31 vs r21) are the same allocation-ordering effect.

Body is structurally complete and instruction-for-instruction equivalent to retail, but three codegen-level facts block byte-exactness: (1) register allocation — retail keeps state ptr=r31, data blob=r30, rodata ptr=r29, seed s16=r28, while both GC/1.3.2 and GC/1.2.5 rank the five cross-call values differently (1.3.2: r31=data/r30=rodata/r29=seed/r28=state; 1.2.5: r31=sprite temp/r30=data/r29=rodata/r28=seed/r27=state), and the ranking is insensitive to every declaration/statement-order permutation tried; (2) the sprite/table loads — retail materialises the sub-table base first (`addi rX,data,0x8E0` then `slwi/lwzx`), my compiles always reassociate the constant into the load displacement (`add rX,base,idx*4; lwz rD,0x8E0(rX)`); (3) the (f32)(s32)counter conversion bias loads `lfd f,0x80(r29)` from rodata, while my builds emit a private literal-pool symbol with an extra lis/addi. GC/1.2.5 scores best on instruction rows (56.4%) but emits the old stmw prologue instead of retail's `_savegpr_27`/psq_stx 1.3.x prologue, so it can never be exact; GC/1.3.2 matches the prologue/frame exactly but scores 53.5%.

Complete and faithful reconstruction (all 8 table-clear loops, the jump-table switch, CARD mount/unmount/serial paths and the 9-arg fn_1_F4810 call are recovered), but the object still needs 13 callee-saved registers (frame 0xb0, _savegpr_19) where retail uses 9 (frame 0xa0, _savegpr_23), so ~700 rows are the same opcodes/operands with different register numbers (loop temps land in r19–r23 instead of r24–r28, `m` in r4 instead of r3); the source-level live-range details that would make MWCC 1.3 reproduce retail's allocation are not recoverable from the disassembly, and no declaration-order/block-scope/helper split moves it.

The reconstruction is structurally complete and compiles, but all remaining differing rows are compiler-internal allocation decisions that source rewrites cannot steer: my callee-saved mapping is entry=r27/handle=r26/dtab=r28/sel=r23/off=r16/tbl=r18/rec=r19 versus the target's clean r31..r14 sequence, and my locals+temporaries region is 0xf0 (frame 0x160) versus the target's 0xe0 (frame 0x150), so every stack offset is shifted; the repeated-expression sqrt/rsqrt blocks, the frame-size probes (declaration reordering, sq/y merging) and the -use_lmw_stmw pragma (which did restore stmw r14) all failed to move either, and only the first ~90 of 2221 diff rows are visible for iteration.

99.6% (6 of 1508 rows). Everything matches byte-for-byte except one scheduling tie-break in the two inlined parse copies used by the odd-n recursion path (parse target = &tmp): retail emits `stb r5,0x38(r1)` (sig.length = i) before the post-loop rescan `lbz r3,0(r6)`, while our compile hoists the rescan load above that store (in the 21 case copies, where the same store goes through the unknown `d` parameter, the order is kept and those copies match exactly). I could not flip this from any source spelling tried: caller-side vs in-helper exp/sign stores, exp/sign store order per branch, parse-only vs wrapper helper, parameter order (d,exp,s)/(s,exp,d), local declaration order, per-branch pointer variable, void* parameter, volatile store/load, recursive-call form, store/load source order, byte-typed store, and value/load reorderings — each either leaves this swap unchanged or worsens other blocks.

Best is the seed (99.6%, GC/1.3.2, 3 rows). The only structural residual is `weight`. Retail does `lwz r21, 0xe4(r1)` for the fctiwz word and then `extsh r4, r21` at the fn_1_4AE0C(lbl_3_data_4B98, weight) call. That means `weight` is a 32-bit local cast with (s16) at the call. The seed's `s16 weight` emits `lwz r0; extsh r21, r0` and a plain `mr r4, r21`. Changing it to `s32 weight` (with `(s16)weight` at the call) fixes that structure exactly. But weight then colours last (r18), where retail has r21 above kind r20 / lbl_3_data_4B84 r19 / fn_3_240DC r18, so 12 register rows differ. Its register does not respond to declaration position (tried before item and before kind), to defining it before kind, or to dropping the (f64) cast. Moving kind ahead of weight breaks the whole allocation. So the s32 weight is probably coloured early only because of its interference degree (survivor law), or it is a web numbered above the locals. Next idea, untried: hold the conversion in a static inline helper's local and call it (`weight = helper(entry)`) so the value numbers above the locals. A helper was added in the last edit, but it is never called, so it is dead code to remove. A GC/1.3.2 capture of the s32 variant would show weight's degree compared with kind's.

The best saved body is still the seed (99.6%, GC/1.3.2, extern-struct pool). Its only residual is the int-to-float bias, which comes from the private @160 pool (lis+lfd) where retail loads lbl_1_rodata_3E48+0x138 off r31. A manual union conversion does not work: it gives fsub+frsp and a new stack slot, which shifts all locals by 8. I then rebuilt the native TU-layout primer: static const tables for 0x0-0x123, a .fzgxpool primer storing 0.0f/1.0f/100.0f/180.0f/32767.0f and (f32)s32, then a static const Word3 {FFFFFFFF,BF800000,FFFFFFFF}. The primer must not contain a (f32)(u32) conversion: the u32 bias would land at 0x138. With the primer, the layout is exact and every pool row is accepted. The last work copy is that primer body plus the RNG written as `n = lbl_801A63C0*K+C; f0 = 180f*((f32)(s32)((n>>16)&0x7FFF)/32767f); lbl_801A63C0 = n;`. Its only remaining diff is 8 rows (adjusted 98.5%) under GC/1.3. All four Word3 default copies match under GC/1.3, but under GC/1.3 the lfd 0x138/lfs 0x134/lfs 0x130 pool loads are scheduled after `stw r3,0(r5)` (the store to lbl_801A63C0), where retail has them right after mullw. Under GC/1.3.2 the RNG loads are hoisted correctly, but the Word3 copies hoist the third lwz above the second stw, so 1.3.2 treats the static const as non-aliasing. Writing the RNG as `lbl_801A63C0 = lbl_801A63C0*K+C` and reading it back avoided the lwzu (addi r5;lwz 0(r5) as in retail). The next attempt should use GC/1.3.2 with the primer and find a way to make the Word3 source alias car stores, perhaps a non-const object placed in .rodata via a section declspec. Or it should use GC/1.3 and find an RNG spelling that hoists the pool loads above the global store.
